transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 mins
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Gibbons (CTO - Saffire), Priya Rao (Lead ML Eng - Saffire), Marcus Hale (Head Ops - Saffire)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on whether Saffire should start on Redwood Hosted (self-serve) vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Main concerns: latency targets for inference at 120ms p95, cost per 1k tokens, data residency, SOC2 and SSO, and a short benchmark to validate latency with their prompt fleet. Agreed next steps include security docs and a small benchmark pilot with 50k credits.

Topics:
- Time-to-first-token / TTFT and credits
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Latency SLOs and benchmarking plan
- Data residency and retention policies

Action items (from call): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): ok everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Maya is our SE, she'll do the technical bits. Alex — you want to intro Saffire quick?
[00:18] Alex (Saffire): yeah thanks, uh yeah I'm Alex, CTO, we run the inference platform for internal tools and customer support automations, looking to move from a bunch of ad-hoc infra to a more predictable inference layer. main drivers are cost and latency.
[00:32] Jordan: perfect, and what's your current infra stack, just rough?
[00:36] Priya (Saffire): we have a mixture — about 8 g4dn-ish nodes right now in cloud, plus some rented TPU time for specific models, but production load is spiky. we've been looking at hosted api options vs reserving capacity.
[00:50] Marcus (Saffire): and we have compliance needs for EU data, some PII redaction, also IAM via Okta SAML, so SSO is a must.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood): got it; that's helpful. today we'll cover quickstart (PLG) flow — free credits, how long TTFT is, and then we can jump into Dedicated/reserved or Private (VPC / on-prem) if you want isolation.
[01:20] Alex: yeah we're curious — like realistically how fast is TTFT? and the free credits — is that enough to validate latency?
[01:28] Jordan: typical TTFT for a small team is <30 minutes to first token — sign up, API key, run sample prompt. with the free credits we can provision 50k tokens which usually covers baseline latency and quality checks. for production you can move to Dedicated.
[01:45] Priya: when you say 30 min is that with a model loaded warm? we worry about cold start for large models, e.g., 70B.
[01:53] Maya: good call. cold starts vary by model size and our runtime. for 7B/13B models it's sub-second instantiation; for 70B we see ~6-12s cold start depending on warm cache and quantization. but we do continuous batching and warm pools for Hosted customers doing steady traffic.
[02:15] Alex: interesting. latency target is 120ms p95 for our chat UI. is that realistic on hosted?
[02:24] Maya: for short sequence lengths and 7B-13B models yes we can hit p95 under 200ms usually; 120ms p95 is tight but achievable with model/quantization choices and a Dedicated pool tuned for your latency SLO. Hosted has multi-tenant tradeoffs; Dedicated gives predictability.
[02:44] Marcus: ok, cost's also critical. can you ballpark cost per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:52] Jordan: rough numbers — hosted gen cost depends on model, but for a 13B-ish it's typically X cents per 1k tokens on hosted; with Dedicated you get lower per-token cost at scale but commit to reserved capacity. i'll send a pricing sheet.
[03:08] Alex: is there an easy path to move from Hosted pilot to Dedicated without reworking the app?
[03:15] Jordan: yes — our serving abstraction keeps the same API. you pin model versions and rollout policies; switching routing to Dedicated is a config change, not code.
[03:24] Priya: about Private — we have some EU-only data that must not leave their region. how does Redwood Private handle data residency and KMS?
[03:33] Maya: Private gives a customer-controlled plane in your VPC, can be deployed in region-specific cluster, integrates with your KMS/HSM. audit logs and retention can be configured per policy. some customers start on Hosted, then move to Private when compliance gating is heavy.
[03:52] Alex: what about PII? we have a lot of PII in prompts, do you offer masking or redaction features?
[03:59] Jordan: we have built-in redact patterns and you can also push to a pre-processing step in your pipeline. we'll share best practice docs.
[04:08] Marcus: security wise, do you have SOC2 and ISO? we need the narrow check for procurement.
[04:13] Jordan: yes SOC2 type II, and we can share the summary and SOC2 report under an NDA. we'll send the security pack after this call.
[04:24] Alex: perfect. for the benchmark, we'd like the test to mimic our chat latency with 100 concurrency and real prompt lengths. can Redwood replicate that?
[04:33] Maya: yes — we can run a benchmark using your prompt set and a synthetic concurrency profile. we recommend starting with a small pilot (500-2k rps bursts) on Hosted to validate model choice, then rerun on Dedicated with fixed nodes to evaluate p95 latency.
[04:52] Priya: note — our prompt distribution is heavy on long contexts, about 512-1024 tokens typical. will that change batching behavior?
[05:01] Maya: longer sequences increase per-token compute and memory; batch sizes will be smaller. KV cache behavior for chat helps some. just flagging — quantization settings also matter for 70B models to fit in memory.
[05:20] Alex: ok. i want to flag vendor lock-in concerns — how portable are model variants?
[05:26] Jordan: our runtime supports ONNX/FLAX/Torch models; we do model-adapter layers to keep API consistent. you can bring your model weights for Dedicated/Private if that matters.
[05:36] Marcus: procurement question — do you support SSO (Okta) + SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:42] Maya: yes SAML/Okta SSO supported, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC roles in Console.
[05:48] Alex: any limits on request rate for hosted during free credits?
[05:52] Jordan: free credits have soft rate limits; we'll set a limit to protect multi-tenant resources but can coordinate a benchmark window where we bump throughput.
[06:04] Priya: one thing, you mentioned KV cache, i heard 'K V cash' in a blog — what's the specifics? like how persistent is it per session?
[06:12] Maya: hah, yeah it's KV cache for attention keys; it's per-short-lived session by default on Hosted, persistent across conversation turns for up to configured TTLs, and Dedicated/Private have extended control.
[06:27] Alex: can we pin models to stay in memory?
[06:30] Maya: Dedicated allows pinned workers and warm pools with faster response. Hosted has warm caches too but not pinned per-customer.
[06:38] Marcus: for the pilot, we want to include a security review. is there a standard package?
[06:43] Jordan: yes we'll attach an SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, key mgmt overview, and SSO docs.
[06:49] Alex: great. other feature question — do you support streaming responses + function/tool calling? we use streaming for token UX.
[06:57] Maya: yes streaming is supported; function calling as well. we can show examples in the quickstart doc.
[07:05] Alex: ok let's talk about timeline — we want a quick pilot this quarter. realistic?
[07:10] Jordan: yes. sign up and TTFT for devs is immediate. pilot timeline: week 1 sign-up and baseline tests, week 2 benchmark and perf tuning, week 3 decision for Dedicated or Private evaluation.
[07:24] Priya: who will be our SE contact for the benchmark?
[07:27] Jordan: Maya will own the benchmark plan and run the first tests. she'll need the prompt set and network profile.
[07:33] Maya: yes i'll put together a test harness and send a small repo. we usually ask for a 100-example seed prompt set and a representative payload.
[07:41] Alex: about costs — can you give a conservative hosted cost estimate for 100k daily tokens?
[07:47] Jordan: it's model dependent; i'll share a pricing sheet but rough hosted generation for 13B could be around $Y/day at 100k tokens. if you plan sustained load, Dedicated reduces unit cost.
[07:59] Marcus: one more ops question — do you support private networking for Dedicated? like can we attach a VPC peering?
[08:06] Maya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private offers full VPC deployments. Dedicated can be in a private subnet with strict egress rules depending on contract.
[08:17] Alex: procurement will ask for SLA info — do you have uptime SLAs?
[08:21] Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract. Hosted has best-effort but very high availability; we'll include SLA overview in the docs.
[08:33] Priya: ok for the benchmark inputs i'll prepare: 1) 100 seed prompts, 2) concurrency profile, 3) sample user IDs and redaction policy.
[08:41] Alex: how do we ensure data isn't retained on your logs beyond retention window?
[08:45] Maya: we have configurable retention and we can disable retention for specific routes; Private gives you more control. we'll send detail on audit logs and retention policy.
[08:57] Marcus: any surprise onboarding costs for Dedicated or Private?
[09:02] Jordan: Dedicated has an onboarding engineering time fee for setting up reserved pools and SSO; Private has larger setup costs due to deployment. we'll include estimates in the pricing doc.
[09:13] Alex: competitor question — we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI — what makes Redwood different?
[09:18] Jordan: we're inference-first with strong tooling for rollout, batching, routing policies, and the ability to move between Hosted/Dedicated/Private with the same API. focus is on production economics.
[09:30] Priya: do you offer quantized model variants? we depend on 4-bit quant for some 70B workloads.
[09:35] Maya: yes we support multiple quantization profiles, and we'll recommend quantization given your memory and latency targets.
[09:42] Alex: ok, what's the handoff for procurement — do you need an MSS or just an SOW?
[09:48] Jordan: for Dedicated/Private we usually do an SOW + enterprise contract; procurement will want SOC2 and the SLA. for Hosted pilot it's self-serve with terms-of-service.
[09:59] Marcus: can we get an explicit list of required customer-side network egress rules for Private?
[10:04] Maya: yes i'll attach a network checklist: ports, CIDR ranges, and KMS endpoints.
[10:11] Alex: cool. is there a way to run a dry-run that mimics our network latency constraints?
[10:17] Maya: we can run the benchmark from our EU region or coordinate on-prem traffic replay; we'll include latency emulation in the plan.
[10:26] Jordan: ok to recap, we'll: send SOC2 and security pack, provision 50k free credits, Maya will draft benchmark plan and repo, Saffire to share prompt set and retention requirements.
[10:40] Alex: yes that's correct. any blockers from our side? procurement wants SLA and docs.
[10:45] Jordan: we'll send those.
[10:47] Priya: quick question — do you support model version pinning and canary rollouts?
[10:51] Maya: yes both; rollouts and traffic split policies are in Console. we can demo that in a short follow-up.
[11:00] Marcus: ok let's schedule the follow-up after you send docs and credits.
[11:05] Jordan: sounds good. i'll send the security pack after this call and provision credits. Maya will email benchmark plan.
[11:11] Alex: thanks all.
[11:13] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up.

End of recording.
